title: ceo-ama-rehearsal-checklist-and-fallback-tree-v0-1
content:
Purpose:
This doc is the working rehearsal checklist and contingency decision tree for the CEO AMA scheduled during the November all-team sync. Primary goals: surface progress on top-level OKRs, enable transparent Q&A, surface product and infra updates, and leave attendees with clear next steps.

Audience & Constraints:
- Audience: whole company (~150 employees), remote-first, 4 timezones (NA/EU/APAC).
- Runtime target: 45 minutes total (+10 min buffer).
- Primary channels: live stream (WebRTC via company meeting infra), live captions, concurrent Slack thread (#all-team-ama), recording posted to Drive within 24h.
- Privacy: no disclosure of unapproved roadmap items or customer PII. Legal on standby.

Roles & RACI (for rehearsal and event):
- CEO (lead): Samantha Lee - narrative + primary Q&A responder.
- Moderator: Avery Patel - queue management, handoffs, time checks.
- Technical backup: Jordan Kim (VP Eng) - handles model/runtime/infra questions and staged demo fallback.
- SRE on-call: Ben Torres - monitors stream health and triggers failover.
- Comms: Priya Narang - announcement, slides, Slack moderation, post-event notes.
- Legal/Security: Maya Ortiz (on standby) - flagged for redirection on sensitive Qs.

Pre-rehearsal checklist (D-5 to D-1):
- D-5: Draft CEO talking points and 2-minute OKR summary. Owner: Samantha.
- D-4: Share slides v1 with leadership; collect comments. Owner: Priya.
- D-3: Tech dry-run of slide deck + demo on staging inference cluster. Owner: Jordan.
- D-2: Full run-through with moderator + SRE; test captions and recording. Owner: Avery + Ben.
- D-1: Final edit of slides; publish to Drive with "locked" permission for presenters; release public agenda. Owner: Priya.
- Rehearsal day: 60–75 minute run-through with scripted intros, demo timing, and Q&A flow. Record rehearsal and note timing deviations.

Tech run checklist (D-3 and rehearsal):
- Stream URL stability check (5 min sustained).
- Recording validated: start/stop, retention policy applied.
- Captions active and verified for speakers.
- Presenter screen share permissions verified.
- Demo environment pinned to a canary Redwood inference endpoint (no production customer keys).
- Network speed baseline: presenters must have 20 Mbps upstream; if below, switch to pre-recorded segment.

Primary event flow (45 min):
- 0:00–05:00 Welcome & logistics (Moderator)
- 05:00–12:00 CEO highlights & 90s per top 3 OKRs (Samantha)
- 12:00–20:00 Product & infra updates (Jordan + brief demo)
- 20:00–40:00 Moderated Q&A (live + Slack-sourced), allocate 2–3 quick redirect slots
- 40:00–45:00 Action items & closing (Samantha + Priya)

Q&A handling policy & queue rules (Moderator):
- Use Slack thread to collect Qs ahead of time and during event. Prioritize: customer-impacting, cross-team blockers, roadmap clarifications, culture/people topics.
- If a question is sensitive/legal, stop and say: "Thanks — we’ll take that offline with the right team" and route to Maya.
- For deep technical questions that would derail time, offer an async follow-up session and tag responder (Jordan).

Fallback decision tree (triggers + actions):
1) Presenter's upstream drop or poor audio/video (trigger: >10s gap or <2 Mbps)
   - Immediate action: Moderator swaps to backup presenter or switches to audio-only.
   - If CEO disconnects for >60s: play 90s pre-recorded CEO intro (hosted on Drive) and continue with product segment.
   - Notify SRE via #ops-oncall with incident note.

2) Entire stream outage (trigger: stream unreachable for >30s and multiple attendees report)
   - Action A (automatic): SRE attempts fast restart of stream endpoint (5–10min).
   - Action B (if restart fails): Move to live Slack thread for Q&A and announce 15–30 minute pause. Use backup Zoom room link and post to #all-team-replay.
   - Postmortem: SRE to file incident in JIRA OPS-9421 with timeline and root cause.

3) Slide leak or unauthorized draft appears publicly during event
   - Action: Comms posts official slide link in Slack with "official" label. Legal evaluates leak; if leak contains sensitive content, legal drafts short statement and coordinates with CEO for follow-up.

4) Host gets unexpected hostile or off-limits question (trigger: policy-sensitive or defamatory)
   - Redirect script: "Appreciate you raising that. That’s a topic our legal/comms teams handle — we’ll follow up offline." Flag the question and route to legal mailbox. No on-the-fly comment beyond redirect.

5) Demo fails (e.g., model returns unexpected behavior or staging unavailable)
   - Swap to recorded demo clip (2–3 minutes) and surface known issue transparently: "We hit a staging problem; prioritizing fix and will update the changelog."
   - Post-event: engineering to file a regression ticket and schedule a 30-minute follow-up demo with interested parties.

Timing slippage rules:
- If Q&A overruns by >8 minutes, moderator triages to top 6 questions and closes live Qs; remaining move to Slack follow-up thread with owners assigned.
- If product segment goes long, cut CEO closing by up to 3 minutes and move remaining items to follow-up notes.

Comms & post-event deliverables (within 24–72 hours):
- Recording + captions uploaded to Drive (Priya, within 24h).
- Slack thread summary with top 10 Qs and canonical answers (Priya + Jordan, 24–48h).
- Action item tracker exported to Confluence page with owners and due dates (Samantha + Ops, 72h).
- Incident report (if any fallback used) with learnings and updated runbook (Ben, within 72h).

Runbook snippets (copyable scripts):
- Stream outage announcement (Moderator): "We’re experiencing technical issues with the livestream. Please follow live updates in #all-team-ama and we expect to resume within 15–30 minutes. Thanks for your patience."
- Sensitive-redirection (Moderator/CEO): "That’s an important topic — we’ll take it offline with the team who owns it and share an update after the event."
- Demo-fail script (Presenter): "We encountered an unexpected issue in staging; we’ll record the failing behavior, file a ticket, and host a follow-up demo next week."

Rehearsal agenda (60–75 minutes recommended):
- 0–05: logistics, intro script confirmation
- 05–20: CEO run-through of slides (stop-for-timing after each OKR blurb)
- 20–35: Product demo with full infra/network checks
- 35–50: Moderator-led simulated Q&A (use seeded questions including edge-cases)
- 50–60: Contingency drill (simulate stream drop, demo fail, hostile Q)
- 60–75: Post-rehearsal notes & action list assignment

Open questions to resolve in next sync:
- Do we want closed captions in additional languages for APAC? (Priya to cost estimate)
- Which OKR metrics will be shown on slides (ops wants confirmed dashboards)? (Jordan to finalize)
- Confirm backup presenter availability window (Samantha to confirm with VP Product).

Notes on tone & framing:
- Prioritize transparency on metrics and blockers without oversharing unvetted roadmap.
- Lean into short, crisp OKR narratives: current state, 6–8 week plan, how attendees can help.
- Celebrate wins and surface concrete asks (e.g., "we need volunteer reviewers for privacy evals — sign up here").

Revision log:
- v0-1 (2025-11-04) initial draft with role assignments and run-through agenda.
- v0-2 (2025-11-07) added fallback tree and rehearsal drills after SRE input.

Action items (owners):
- Samantha: finalize 90s OKR blurbs (due 2025-11-05).
- Priya: publish final slides and Slack announcement (due 2025-11-06).
- Jordan: prep demo recording and staging pin (due 2025-11-06).
- Ben: validate stream restart playbook and test incident path (due 2025-11-05).

End of doc.
